verdict.line: You lose if you stand in Infernal Chains and eat the follow-up Q3; you win if you wall him off with W and outscale through items.

brief.thesis: This matchup is a trade-pattern puzzle, not a stat check: Yorick vs Aatrox sits at 49.2% over 1,345 games, dead even, but OP.GG flags Aatrox as the solo-kill threat because his E (Umbral Dash)-into-Q (The Darkin Blade) combo punishes you for standing still. Your W (Dark Procession) directly answers this by blocking his dash path or his retreat, which is the single biggest lever you have in lane.

theirWindow.when: E (Umbral Dash) is up, he's closing distance
theirWindow.what: He is setting up his E-into-Q combo. Don't greed an auto trade here; back off or pre-place W (Dark Procession) to cut his dash line before he closes.

yourWindow.when: his E (Umbral Dash) just went on cooldown (9-5s)
yourWindow.what: Walk up and trade freely with Q (Last Rites) — he has no gap closer or disengage for the full cooldown window, so this is your safest extended trade.

start.why: Picked in 47.6% over 804 games; the sustain and poke-reduction blunts his early auto trades while his E-Q combo is still clumsy to land.

boots.why: 71.2% pick rate at 50% win rate; the physical damage reduction directly softens his Q slams and his passive-empowered autos.

core.why: Core first item across both top build paths; the stat stick and proc damage close the trade-damage gap his passive heal creates.
Appears in the 61.5%-winrate path; the armor shred stacks with your E (Mourning Mist) armor reduction to make your sustained trades hit harder.
Common in every listed core path; ability haste shortens your Q (Last Rites) and E (Mourning Mist) cooldowns for more frequent pokes.

runes.keystoneWhy: Rewards the extended trades you want once his E (Umbral Dash) is down on cooldown; Triumph and Last Stand keep you alive through his passive sustain in close fights.
runes.alt: Master-tier Yorick players (5,865 games) run Grasp of the Undying instead — better for a player who expects to get outtraded early and wants sustain through his E-Q combo rather than winning the all-in.

summoners.why: The 52.3%-winrate Flash+Ignite page is the strongest performer here; Ignite punishes his Deathbringer Stance heal directly and denies the sustain that lets him win extended trades.

playing.title: Hold W for his dash, not for damage
playing.detail: Dark Procession's wall is your counter to Umbral Dash. Save it to block his escape or his engage line rather than using it purely as a damage-block.

playing.title: Trade only when his E is down
playing.detail: His E (Umbral Dash) passively heals him on champion damage and gives him the dash for his combo. Track its cooldown (9/8/7/6/5s) and only commit auto trades in that window.

playing.title: Poke with E before closing in
playing.detail: Mourning Mist's armor shred and slow set up your all-in. Throw it first, then walk in once he's marked and weakened, per OP.GG's own read on this lane.

playing.title: Respect his Q3 return swing
playing.detail: The Darkin Blade can swing three times with different areas each time. If you get hit by the first swing, back off rather than trading through all three.

playing.title: Track Deathbringer Stance readiness
playing.detail: His passive empowers his next auto with bonus magic damage and healing on a cycle. Avoid standing in an extended auto-trade right when it's clearly about to proc.

playing.title: Don't contest his R all-in without summoners
playing.detail: World Ender gives him AD, healing, and move speed, and extends on a takedown. If he pops it, disengage rather than try to out-damage the healing boost.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, boots, and summoner spells above are pulled directly from measured OP.GG games on the current patch (16.19.1); the trade-pattern reasoning and power-curve calls are my own tactical read.

stats.opponentTip: Avoid Aatrox’s (E)-(Q) combo. If hit by his combo, move around to avoid his follow up (Q) and trap him inside [W] to retreat. Use [E] to poke and close in once he is low on health.
